status: Original static evidence only; no public reachability, complete phase parity, or TARGET-01.2 closure claim.
address_convention: Findings use module-relative RVAs; original Ghidra exports use virtual addresses. Instruction sites are distinguished from containing functions.

findings.claim: d0168 target setup subscribes Attack to d0196 and sets active flag4.

sites.meaning: CALL Agent_SubscribeArrival 0561f0 on enabled Move branch

findings.claim: d016f dispatch passes (0,0,0) to Move_HandleTargetTask; arg08 zero removes Move's own arrival subscription. Attack remains arrival receiver.
Arrival validates the current target then starts/retries swing; it does not pop d016f or clear active4.

Ordinary cooldown-positive early return, range chase, facing chase, animation start and mover stop in495180 do not pop retained d016f.49a240 starts a physical request and subscribes Attack arrival without adding/popping logical tasks.
Normal swing completion retains d016f and restarts range or facing chase. The flags800 finishing-wait branch instead clears800 and pops the current d016a; AttackOnce uses recovery.
Recovery task-pop returns true only after removing d016f, optionally preceded by d0168 and d0163. d016a is untouched/false; d0169 is popped/false.
Recovery rechecks active4 after release callbacks, invokes task-pop, clears4, then only on eligible pop may create D051 and dispatch successor.
Generic non-preserved cleanup independently clears active4 after target release and reset.

engine_mapping_limits: A physical group is not the retained d016f owner; group absence cannot determine pop eligibility.
Reaction can be d0163 above d016f; ordinary walk/facing/melee/ranged/cooldowns retain d016f. Finishing wait and already-created point recovery are distinct logical tasks.
This mapping is an implementation guide, not proof that any current C phase name alone reproduces every native queue composition.
Suspension, replacement and reentrant callbacks require actual retained task identity; not inferred from currentmove.proc.
Ghidra historical comments are retained in the raw export as annotations, not independent evidence.
